items.title: Unheard. Unserved: Black women face added health care barriers as race, gender intersect
items.description: In the final installment of the Global News' series Unheard. Unserved, we look how gender and race can intersect to create even deeper gaps in treatment and outcomes for women.

items.title: Alberta food banks grapple with high cost of free beef
items.description: Rural Alberta food banks are seeking provincial funding to support a program that sees cattle producers donate animals to organizations that feed people in need.

items.title: Greenwashing laws are changing. Businesses are relieved, but environmentalists have concerns
items.description: Laws about greenwashing — making a false or misleading statement about the environmental benefits of a product — will remain on the books, but the Liberal government has said it will be making changes aimed at offering businesses more certainty about what runs afoul of the law.

items.title: Yoplait Yop yogurt drinks recalled in Canada over plastic contamination fears
items.description: Many of Yoplait's yogurts have been pulled from Canadian shelves after the company shared fears over pieces of plastic in some products.

items.title: Reported illnesses have tripled in some school districts. Experts say mental health is a factor
items.description: A CBC investigation finds that school time lost due to reported illness is up in all districts that provided data — more than tripling in some places compared to five years ago. While the data doesn’t say why, experts say deteriorating mental health is causing some kids to stay home.

items.title: Carney says he'll speak with Trump ‘when it's appropriate'
items.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he doesn't have a "burning issue" to speak with President Donald Trump and would speak with him "when it's appropriate."

items.title: Azizi, beloved lion at Moncton zoo, remembered as gentle prankster
items.description: Moncton zoo visitors have fond memories of Azizi, an African lion. Azizi was euthanized this week due to declining health.

items.title: Manitoba Government Adds $1 Million to Accelerate Construction of Park Community Centre and Child-Care Facility in Brandon
‘Do your research, advocate': Alberta radio host with brain cyst says long consult wait shows rural care gaps
items.description: Alberta radio host Kim Johnston says his worsening symptoms and a months-long wait for a neurosurgery consult show how specialist delays are straining rural health care.

items.title: Trailblazing N.L. pitcher Jaida Lee drafted in new Women’s Pro Baseball League
items.description: Nineteen-year-old Jaida Lee of St. John's was drafted to play for New York in the Women’s Pro Baseball League on Thursday night.

items.title: Plug-in polluter? Why Canada may need to rethink 'transition' EV
items.description: Plug-in hybrid cars are a compromise for people wanting range with electric capability. But new research finds they’re less green than you think — so how should they fit into a zero-emissions future?

items.title: Some Yoplait YOP drinkable yogurt recalled in Canada due to plastic pieces
items.description: A nationwide recall has been issued for some YOP drinkable yogurt products after Yoplait Canada cautioned of the presence of plastic pieces.

Annual Stuff A Bus helps address growing need at Calgary Food Bank
items.description: Calgarians donated food items on Saturday for the annual Stuff A Bus campaign in support of the Calgary Food Bank. This year is more important than ever, according to organizers.

items.title: On Our Radar: Buddie turns its completely understandable stress into something beautiful
items.description: Guitar bands are back in Vancouver, and it’s beautiful.

items.title: Carney says ‘constructive' talks ongoing with Alberta about oil pipeline
items.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday addressed speculation about whether an agreement is close for a new pipeline between Alberta and B.C.'s northern coast.

items.title: Retailers feel Black Friday pressure as Canadians expected to tighten their spending
items.description: With trade uncertainty, tariffs and rising prices, Canadian shoppers are expected to pull back this holiday season. Retailers are offering weeks-long discounts —and for some, their first Black Friday deals ever — in the hope of enticing people to spend.

Small Sask. town rallies to preserve historic bridge a decade after its closure
items.description: The town of Saint Louis, Sask., has rallied together to save a historic bridge with a century-old legacy. The former railway bridge is now a walkway designed to teach people about the community's rich Métis culture.
